reflections.title: "Under Whose Wings You Have Taken Refuge"

reflect.text: When deep loss and sorrow strike, we can easily feel forgotten or grow bitter. Yet Ruth chose to step forward in faith and place her trust under the protective wings of the Lord. What felt like coincidences—finding a safe field and meeting Boaz—were actually God tenderly guiding her steps to begin a story of restoration.

Much of Ruth's faithful devotion to Naomi had been quiet, hard, everyday work that the wider world never noticed. But Boaz’s blessing shows that nothing done in secret escapes God’s sight. The Lord sees our unseen labor, our hidden tears, and our faithful service, and He honors every quiet step taken for Him.

Knowing that God sees us and shelters us under His wings gives us strength to keep going. We do not need the praise of the crowd, nor do we need to despair when life is hard. God is still at work in the quiet details of our lives, and He never forgets those who seek refuge in Him.

questions: In what areas of quiet service or unseen struggle do you need to remember that God sees you?
How can sheltering under God's wings bring you peace when circumstances feel overwhelming?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for sheltering us under Your wings when we face loss or weariness. Help us to trust that You see all our unseen work and that You are guiding our steps each day. Give us endurance and steady faith, knowing You never forget us. Amen.

reflections.title: Finding Grace in the Field

reflect.text: Ruth simply set out to gather food provided for the needy, yet her steps led straight to Boaz. While it might have looked like pure chance, God’s sovereign care guided her every move. Boaz did not merely meet the bare minimum of the law. Instead, he welcomed Ruth with lavish generosity, protecting her and ensuring she had more than enough grain.

At mealtime, Boaz invited Ruth to eat roasted grain until she was fully satisfied, with food left over. In an even greater way, Christ invites us to feast upon His kindness. When we come to Jesus, He satisfies our hungry souls completely. His mercy removes our guilt, fills our minds with truth, and gives us peace, leaving us with an endless supply of love to spare.

Like Ruth, we are invited to glean daily in God’s rich field of promises. A good gleaner stoops low in humility, gathers single ears of truth one by one, and holds onto them tightly. When we come to God’s Word with a humble heart and an eager appetite, we discover plenty of comfort to sustain our souls.

questions: In what ways have you experienced God’s quiet guidance in what seemed like ordinary, everyday moments?
How can you approach God's Word with a humble, watchful heart to glean His promises today?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You that our lives are guided by Your loving care rather than blind chance. Thank You for meeting us with lavish kindness in Christ and satisfying our deepest hunger. Teach us to walk humbly in Your fields, treasuring every promise You have given us. Amen.
